title: How To Fix the “Kernel Security Check Failure” Error in Windows 10? - GeeksforGeeks
content:
Encountering the Kernel Security Check Failure error on Windows 10 can be frustrating, especially when it leads to a Blue Screen of Death (BSOD). This error typically points to system files, drivers, or memory issues. In this guide, we'll walk you through the steps to fix Kernel Security Check Failure on Windows 10 and provide effective solutions to resolve this Windows 10 blue screen error. Whether you're facing this issue due to outdated drivers or corrupt files, these troubleshooting methods can help you get your system back on track.

Table of Content

  • Method 1: Use Windows Safe Mode to Fix Security Kernel Check Failure
  • Method 2: Fix Security Kernel Check Failure by checking Memory Issues
  • Method 3: Run Hard Drive Diagnostic
  • Method 4: Update Disk Driver
  • Method 5: Fix Security Kernel Check Error by using System File Checker
  • Method 6: Scan for any Potential Virus and Threat on Windows
  • Method 7: Check for any Pending Windows "Update & Security"

What is Windows Security Kernel Check Failure?

On Windows 10, over 500 recorded Common Windows Issues occur with the Windows Blue Screen Death. That is the reason, these errors are termed as the BSOD Error on Windows. The KERNEL_SECURITY_CHECK_FAILURE on Windows is one of the BSOD Errors that can start at the time of booting of the device when the OS is being called.

Hardware & Software-related causes are present behind the Windows KERNEL_SECURITY_CHECK_FAILURE Issue. However, the problem with the software is the major reason behind the BSOD Issue. Some of the reasons behind the Windows Kernel Error are the following.

  • The Hard drive or the driver becomes corrupted as it is not updated.
  • Sometimes, the Windows Drivers become outdated to run the system.
  • Any Virus or Malware can affect the system execution.
  • Various kinds of Software Memory Issues can be a reason.
  • Windows Update-related issues might be a cause of the problem.

Methods to Fix the Security Kernel Check in Windows 10

To security kernel check failure in Windows, we have compiled a list of the following methods that are worthful to be executed. All the users need to follow the mentioned methods properly to resolve the actual problem. Let's start with executing on Windows Safe Mode.

Method 1: Use Windows Safe Mode to Fix Security Kernel Check Failure

Safe Mode is probably one of the best method to recover any system failure. Below are the simple steps to enter the safe mode.

Step 1: Enter Boot Menu & Go to Advanced Option

On the Windows Boot Menu, go for the Troubleshoot Option.

Step 2: Go to Startup Settings

Click on the Startup Settings option.

Step 3: Enter Safe Mode

At last, press any Key related to the Windows Safe Mode to start the service.

Method 2: Fix Security Kernel Check Failure by checking Memory Issues

You may also check for security failure through Windows Memory Diagnostic run.

Step 1: Open Search Box & type 'Windows Memory Diagnostics"

Search for the Windows Memory Diagnostic & open the option.

Step 2: Click to Restart

Click on the Restart Now & Check For Problems option.

Method 3: Run Hard Drive Diagnostic

Running the CHKDSK utility helps check and repair hard drive errors and keeps your system data organized.

Step 1: Go to Run & open Command Prompt

Search for the Command Prompt on the Search Bar & open it.

Step 2: Check for Hard Drive health

Execute the following command that will check the health of the Hard Drive & fix it if any problem is there.

Command: chkdsk C: /f

Method 4: Update Disk Driver

Outdated drivers are also among those reason to create issue with the Kernal Security Failure.

Step 1: Open Driver Manager

Open the Device Manager by simply making a right-click on the Start Symbol.

Step 2: Select "Update Driver"

Then, search for the Driver under the Disk Section & click on the Update Driver option to get the latest version.

Step 3: Search for Automatic Driver Updates

Click on the option Search Automatically For Driver for installation of the latest possible driver.

Method 5: Fix Security Kernel Check Error by using System File Checker

Using this method, you can easily run for SFC scan which will fetch if any issue persists.

Step 1: Click Windows and Open Command Prompt

Open the Command Prompt by searching on the Search Bar.

Step 2: Run Windows System File Checker Scan

Now, the following command needs to be executed on the CMD. It will check all the files & find out possible issues there.

Command: sfc/ scannow

Method 6: Scan for any Potential Virus and Threat on Windows

Windows OS provides you an option to check for any Potential Virus and Threats.

Step 1: Check for Updates & Security

Open Windows Settings & click on the Update & Security option.

Step 2: Look for any Potential Threat

Click on the Virus & Threat Protection option after that.

Step 3: Run a Quick Scan

Then, select the option Quick Scan to start the scan process.

Method 7: Check for any Pending Windows "Update & Security"

You may also run a scan to check for any pending updates.

Step 1: Open the Settings & click on Update and Security option.

Step 2: Check for Any Pending Updates

Under Windows Update, click on the Check For Updates option.

By following these steps, users can resolve their internal system issues without getting any internal or external errors.

Important Note:

1. Ensure to disable any third-party antivirus (if you have). This might also create an issue with your Windows. Once you disable or uninstall it, reboot your PC to check the issue still persist.

2. There might be a chance that your Windows OS might have impacted due to any third-party apps or some other reason. So, the best way could be to perform a fresh Windows Installation and if the problem still persist then you might reconsider it by checking the RAM or hard disk for corruption.

Conclusion

Fixing the Kernel Security Check Failure error on Windows 10 is essential to maintaining your system's stability. By following these steps to resolve Kernel Security Check Failure, you'll be able to address the root causes such as incompatible drivers or hardware issues. Regular system maintenance and keeping your software up to date can prevent future Kernel Security Check stop code errors and ensure your computer runs smoothly.
